overview: Colonial Motor Company (CMC), founded in 1919 and NZX-listed since 1962, owns and operates a network of franchised motor-vehicle dealerships across New Zealand, anchored by 12 Ford dealerships (7 also carrying Mazda), alongside Southpac Trucks (Kenworth/DAF heavy trucks), Agricentre South (New Holland/Case IH tractors), JAC Motors, an expanding BYD electric-vehicle representation (via subsidiaries Energy Motors in Taranaki and Adventure Motor Group in Canterbury/Wairarapa), and a range of other light-vehicle, motorcycle and parts/service franchises. A structurally important part of the business is CMC's large freehold property portfolio of dealership land and buildings, which it owns, develops and leases to its own operating subsidiaries at market rates, meaning a meaningful share of shareholder value sits in real estate rather than retail trading margin. The company is tightly held, with the Gibbons family (descendants of the founding family) collectively holding over 60% of shares, resulting in thin free float and low trading liquidity; CEO Alex Gibbons leads day-to-day operations under Chairman Ashley Waugh.

business_model.summary: CMC earns most of its revenue selling new and used vehicles, trucks and tractors through owned dealership subsidiaries, supplemented by parts, service and workshop revenue that acts as a profit ballast through the cycle, plus finance/insurance commissions on vehicle sales. Layered on top is an internal property business: CMC owns the freehold land and buildings under most of its dealerships and charges its own subsidiaries market rents, so consolidated results blend automotive retail margin with property income and periodic revaluation gains.

revenue_streams.name: Products (new & used vehicles, trucks, tractors, parts)
revenue_streams.trend: cyclical - FY2026 group revenue ~$1.07bn (+6.8% YoY), though H2 FY2026 mix shifted toward NEVs after a Middle East oil-shock disrupted demand for diesel/ICE vehicles

revenue_streams.name: Services (workshop, servicing, F&I-related)
revenue_streams.trend: growing steadily, more resilient than vehicle sales; FY2025 $89.13m vs $80.98m FY2023; H1-2026 $47.2m vs $45.5m H1-2025

revenue_streams.name: Other income (incl. property-related)
revenue_streams.trend: stable, plus periodic property fair-value gains recognised separately below the trading line

business_model.customer_type: B2C retail vehicle buyers plus B2B fleet, agribusiness and commercial trucking customers
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand only, but geographically diversified with a North Island Metro vs South Island/Rural split that management explicitly calls out as a 'two-speed economy' - North Island metro markets have been weaker than South Island and rural/agribusiness-linked markets through FY2025-FY2026, with agri-sector strength (dairy, red meat) continuing to support tractor and implement sales

main_competitors: Andrew Simms/other independent Ford-Mazda dealer groups
Manheim/other truck importers for Southpac's Kenworth/DAF business
Chinese OEM-affiliated dealer networks (BYD, GWM, MG, Chery, Zeekr, Jaecoo, Geely, Dongfeng and others - now over a dozen Chinese brands in the NZ market)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest Ford dealer groups in New Zealand (Ranger was the #1-selling vehicle nationally for 10 consecutive years through 2024, lost the top spot to the Toyota RAV4 in calendar 2025, then reclaimed #1 in the ute/commercial segment through H1 calendar 2026 and again in July 2026); niche leadership in Kenworth/DAF heavy trucks via Southpac and in New Holland/Case IH tractors via Agricentre South (after divesting Kubota in Nov 2025 to focus on core franchises); now also a growing multi-region BYD dealer partner

moat_factors.description: Unlike many auto retailers that lease dealership sites, CMC owns much of its land and buildings, giving balance-sheet resilience, capital-appreciation upside and control over prime dealership real estate in growth corridors; management highlighted a materially strengthened balance sheet in FY2026 driven by significantly lower inventory levels and reduced borrowings

Multi-decade Ford New Zealand relationships and status as the largest single Ford dealer group provide scale in parts/service and negotiating position with the OEM, though the franchise itself is owned by Ford, not CMC

Spread across Ford/Mazda light vehicles, Kenworth/DAF trucks, agricultural equipment, JAC Motors and now BYD reduces reliance on any single brand or regional economy, evidenced by rural/agribusiness strength offsetting North Island metro weakness and by continued BYD dealership expansion into Canterbury and Wairarapa during FY2026

Services revenue has grown steadily and is far less cyclical than new-vehicle sales, cushioning downturns; Southpac's Truck Related Parts (TRP) network also expanded (new Nelson and Dunedin stores) even while new truck sales stayed weak through FY2026

Gibbons family ownership >60% supports a multi-generational, conservative capital allocation approach (steady/growing dividend policy, disciplined property investment) but also limits the influence of minority shareholders; insiders (including Graeme and James Gibbons) have been net buyers of stock over the past year

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on Ford, and specifically the Ranger ute, for volume and profit - any Ford NZ model transition, allocation change or share loss directly hits earnings, and CEO Alex Gibbons himself has warned the current 'multi-layer of competition has taken the market to an unsustainable level' in NZ, implying further margin pressure ahead of an expected brand consolidation

Southpac's heavy-truck business faced a broadly flat year to 30 June 2026 and management expects several 'leaner' sales months in H1 FY2027 while managing the DAF model runout and transition to the Next Generation DAF range, even as early recovery signs emerge for calendar 2027
Thin free float and low share liquidity make the stock difficult for institutions to trade and can lead to persistent valuation discounts or premiums disconnected from fundamentals

Chinese EV/PHEV exposure via BYD (Energy Motors Taranaki, Adventure Motors BYD Canterbury/Wairarapa) is small-scale relative to the scale of the competitive threat - over a dozen Chinese brands have entered NZ within two years, straining margins market-wide and forcing CMC to warn of an 'unsustainable' level of competition

Low reported net margins (trading profit after tax of ~1.7-1.8% of revenue in FY2026) typical of vehicle distribution, leaving limited room to absorb further volume/margin pressure without cost actions; H2 FY2026 was additionally disrupted by a Middle East conflict/oil-price shock that shifted demand away from the group's diesel-weighted inventory toward new-energy vehicles it was not fully positioned to supply

growth_drivers: Cyclical recovery in NZ new-vehicle registrations - market up double digits YTD through mid-2026 before a Middle East-driven oil shock disrupted the trajectory in H2 FY2026; passenger segment registrations remained the strongest performer (e.g. August 2026 passenger registrations +13% YoY) even as commercial/ute registrations slid
Refreshed group-wide focus on used-vehicle sales, which management credits as a key driver of resilience through FY2025-FY2026 and which 'remained robust' even through the disrupted H2 FY2026

New model cycle across the portfolio - Ford Ranger Hybrid, Mazda 6e and CX-6e battery-electric models, a JAC T9 plug-in hybrid ute, and the Next Generation DAF truck range are all due through FY2027, directly targeting the shift in demand toward new-energy vehicles that the oil shock accelerated

Expanding BYD representation - Adventure Motor Group's new dealerships in Canterbury and Wairarapa (agreed 30 June 2026) plus the existing Energy Motors BYD dealership in Taranaki give CMC direct participation in the fastest-growing segment of the NZ new-vehicle market rather than ceding it entirely to independent Chinese-brand networks

Ongoing property development programme - completed Fagan Motors (Masterton) rebuild, new Avon City Ford facility in Rangiora, land banked in Queenstown, a new Southpac facility in Palmerston North, and Hutchinson Motors' new Detroit Place facility in Christchurch - expanding capacity and adding to the freehold portfolio
New franchise wins - securing the Mitsubishi franchise in Manukau (May 2025, trading as Manukau Autos) and the BYD expansion (June 2026) show continued opportunistic franchise/dealership expansion

Southpac's growing Truck Related Parts (TRP) network (new stores in Nelson and Dunedin) extending the more resilient parts/service annuity into the truck segment, with management citing early signs of a genuine heavy-truck fleet-replacement recovery building into 2027 as post-COVID supply-chain disruption has fully unwound

Agribusiness/dairy tailwind - strong dairy payout and improving red meat returns continuing to drive a tractor-market recovery for Agricentre South after Kubota was divested (Nov 2025) to focus on core New Holland/Case IH franchises

Materially strengthened balance sheet exiting FY2026 (lower inventory, reduced borrowings) gives CMC flexibility to fund the coming wave of NEV dealership investment and further property development from a position of strength

business.description: Ford dealerships (12 of the group's ~19+ outlets) and the Ranger model in particular are central to group profitability; light-commercial/ute demand has been the softer segment through 2026 even as Ranger has periodically reclaimed the #1 sales spot

National truck volumes were broadly flat in the year to 30 June 2026; management expects several leaner months in H1 FY2027 during the DAF model transition, with only 'early signs' of a genuine recovery building for 2027

business.risk: Chinese OEM competitive entry / margin compression
business.description: Over a dozen Chinese brands have entered the NZ market within two years, each pursuing aggressive expansion; CEO Alex Gibbons explicitly warned in the September 2026 annual report that this 'multi-layer of competition has taken the market to an unsustainable level that will result in brand consolidation' - implying continued near-term margin pressure across new and used vehicle sales before any relief from consolidation materialises; CMC's own BYD dealership push mitigates but does not eliminate cannibalisation risk to its core Ford network

The Middle East conflict and resulting oil-price shock in H2 FY2026 abruptly shifted customer demand toward new-energy vehicles; CMC's inventory positioning (diesel/ICE-weighted) could not quickly adapt, directly denting H2 FY2026 trading performance - illustrating vulnerability to sudden geopolitical/commodity shocks

Prior years' commentary flagged high industry-wide inventory levels pressuring margins; FY2026 saw inventory levels reduced significantly, improving the balance sheet, though a crowded market with too many brands importing vehicles remains a structural risk to industry-wide margins

financial.description: A large, low-margin inventory base is funded substantially by floorplan finance; a sharp demand drop can strand inventory and squeeze liquidity, though FY2026 saw borrowings reduced alongside lower inventory, improving the position entering FY2027

Interest expense fell through FY2025 and H1-2026 as OCR cuts flowed through and borrowings were paid down; the business benefits materially from rate declines and is correspondingly exposed if rates rise again

financial.risk: Weak NZ dollar / FX and oil-price shocks
financial.description: Imported vehicles/parts are priced in foreign currency; the H2 FY2026 Middle East conflict and associated oil-price shock is a direct example of an external shock disrupting trading conditions and demand mix with limited notice

regulatory.description: Although the Clean Car Discount feebate was repealed from 1 January 2024, the Clean Car Standard importer CO2 targets remain in force, requiring OEMs/importers to blend in more low-emission vehicles or pay penalties, which can affect model mix, pricing and availability

A prior Government decision to remove tax depreciation on commercial buildings drove a one-off non-cash deferred tax charge of $12.7m in FY2024 that crushed reported (non-trading) profit despite stable trading profit - illustrates how tax-policy changes on CMC's large property base can distort reported earnings without affecting cash flow

macro.risk: Geopolitical shocks (Middle East conflict / oil price)
macro.description: A Middle East conflict that began in late February 2026 produced an oil-price shock and supply disruption that materially disrupted H2 FY2026 trading and shifted demand toward new-energy vehicles faster than CMC's inventory could adapt; ongoing geopolitical volatility remains an explicit management-cited risk to FY2027

macro.risk: NZ consumer/business confidence and OCR path
macro.description: New-vehicle demand is highly correlated with interest rates and general economic conditions; management continues to describe a 'two-speed economy' with weaker North Island metro/truck markets versus more resilient South Island/rural and agribusiness-linked demand, and frames FY2027 as a 'slowly improving' economy rather than a robust recovery

Agricentre South's tractor sales and part of the broader commercial vehicle base are geared to farm-gate returns; a downturn in dairy payout or red meat prices would remove a current offsetting tailwind
Heavy truck volumes are a leading indicator of broader freight/economic activity; FY2026 volumes were flat and management only cites 'early signs' of optimism for 2027, not a confirmed recovery

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The NZ new-vehicle market saw a strong cyclical recovery through calendar H1 2026 (registrations up double digits year-to-date), but a Middle East conflict and associated oil-price shock beginning in late February 2026 disrupted the second half, shifting demand mix toward new-energy vehicles. Passenger registrations have remained comparatively resilient (e.g. August 2026 +13% YoY) while commercial/ute registrations have been softer. The market is also increasingly crowded, with over a dozen Chinese brands now competing for share, which CMC's own CEO has characterised as reaching an 'unsustainable' level likely to trigger consolidation.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - new-vehicle sales are strongly discretionary, rate-sensitive and now also exposed to geopolitical/commodity shocks that can rapidly shift demand mix (as shown by the H2 FY2026 oil shock); parts/service and property income are comparatively non-cyclical and provide earnings ballast
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - both directly (floorplan/vehicle finance funding costs) and indirectly (consumer/business willingness to finance vehicle, truck and tractor purchases); OCR cuts through 2025-26 have been a tailwind, reflected in reduced FY2026 borrowings and interest costs
key_input_costs: Imported vehicle costs (FX-exposed, NZD-denominated pricing on USD/JPY/EUR/RMB sourced product)
Oil/fuel prices (now a more visible driver of demand mix after the H2 FY2026 shock)
Building/construction costs for dealership and NEV-related development
Staff remuneration - the second-largest expense line after cost of products sold

recent_developments.event: Released 108th Annual Report (year to 30 June 2026) to NZX; FY2026 trading profit after tax of $18.7m, up 4.7% on FY2025's $17.8m, on revenue up 6.8% to ~$1.07bn; final dividend of 25.0cps declared (record date 25-Sep-2026, paid 5-Oct-2026), taking the total FY2026 dividend to 40.0cps (70% of trading profit), up from 35.0cps in FY2025

CEO Alex Gibbons warned in the annual report that over a dozen Chinese vehicle brands have entered the NZ market within two years, taking competition to an 'unsustainable level that will result in brand consolidation' in a small market like New Zealand, citing margin pressure across new and used vehicle sales

A Middle East conflict began, producing an oil-price shock and supply disruption that Chairman Ashley Waugh said was unfavourably timed for the group, shifting customer demand toward new-energy vehicles faster than CMC's largely diesel/ICE-weighted inventory could adapt, disrupting H2 FY2026 trading

Balance sheet materially strengthened relative to the two prior years via significantly lower inventory levels and reduced external borrowings; used-vehicle trading remained robust throughout the disrupted period

Southpac Trucks: heavy-truck market broadly flat for the year to 30 June 2026; management cited early signs of optimism for calendar 2027 as economic activity begins lifting fleet-replacement demand, though several 'leaner' sales months are expected in H1 FY2027 during the DAF model runout and transition to the Next Generation DAF range; Southpac's independent-dealer parts and service network continues to grow

Agreed with BYD Auto NZ (a division of the Ateco Group) to expand BYD representation via subsidiary Adventure Motor Group Limited, establishing new dealerships 'Adventure Motors BYD Canterbury' (south Christchurch) and 'Adventure Motors BYD Wairarapa', with further locations flagged; complements the existing Energy Motors BYD dealership in Taranaki

H1-2026 result: trading profit after tax of $10.4-10.7m, up ~50-55% YoY, described as 'appreciably better' than anticipated at the November 2025 AGM; interim dividend held at 15.0cps, paid 30 March 2026
Agricentre South sold its Kubota business (including the North Road, Invercargill property) to focus on core New Holland and Case IH heavy tractor franchises
2025 Annual Meeting held in Wellington; AGM resolutions passed, Chair's and CEO's addresses released to NZX
FY2025 full-year result: trading profit after tax $17.8m (broadly flat vs FY2024's $17.9m) in a 'patchy' market; total FY2025 dividend held at 35.0cps (64% payout ratio), matching FY2024
Secured the Mitsubishi franchise for Manukau, South Auckland, establishing 'Manukau Autos' on the Bakerfield Place site

Model launches flagged for FY2027 across the portfolio to meet the NEV demand shift: Mazda 6e and CX-6e battery-electric models, Ford Ranger Hybrid, a JAC T9 plug-in hybrid ute, and the Next Generation DAF truck range
2026 Annual Meeting scheduled for midday, Friday 6 November 2026, at the Harbourside Function Venue, Wellington, per the Notice of Meeting mailed with the 108th Annual Report

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Report (21 September 2026); H1 FY2026 result (26 February 2026)

items.target: Several 'leaner' sales months expected during the DAF model runout and transition to the Next Generation DAF range
items.notes: Framed alongside 'early signs' of optimism for a genuine fleet-replacement recovery building into calendar 2027, but management is explicit the near-term months will be softer due to model-transition disruption

items.target: Expect further margin pressure and eventual brand consolidation as the market reaches an 'unsustainable' number of competing brands
items.vs_prior: new, more explicit caveat than prior years
items.notes: CEO Alex Gibbons' clearest public statement yet that current industry-wide competitive intensity (over a dozen Chinese brands within two years) cannot persist without some players exiting or merging

items.target: Multiple new NEV launches across Ford, Mazda, JAC and DAF through FY2027 to meet the demand shift accelerated by the H2 FY2026 oil shock
items.notes: Management explicitly positioning the group 'to adapt to ongoing geopolitical volatility and a slowly improving New Zealand economy' via faster NEV portfolio expansion

items.target: FY2026 total dividend of 40.0cps (70% of trading profit after tax), up from 35.0cps (64%) in FY2025
items.notes: Payout ratio increased materially alongside the modest trading profit growth, signalling Board confidence in the strengthened balance sheet; long track record of holding or growing the payout through the cycle

items.target: No explicit numeric target, but management flagged a materially stronger balance sheet (lower inventory, reduced borrowings) entering FY2027, providing capacity to fund NEV dealership investment and property development
items.notes: Qualitative balance-sheet guidance rather than a numeric target, consistent with CMC's practice of not issuing formal earnings guidance

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Ashley Waugh described FY2026 as a 'satisfying and respectable outcome' given a disrupted trading environment, noting the Middle East conflict beginning in late February 2026 produced an oil shock and supply disruption whose timing was 'unfavourable' for the group's diesel-weighted inventory positioning, shifting demand toward new-energy vehicles faster than the group could adapt. He highlighted a materially strengthened balance sheet (significantly lower inventory, reduced external borrowings) and reiterated that used-vehicle trading remained robust throughout. CEO Alex Gibbons struck a more cautionary competitive tone, warning that over a dozen Chinese brands have entered NZ within two years and that the resulting 'multi-layer of competition has taken the market to an unsustainable level that will result in brand consolidation for a small market like New Zealand' - while noting established brands retain advantages via reputation and dealer networks. On trucks, Gibbons cited early signs of optimism for a 2027 fleet-replacement recovery as post-COVID supply-chain disruption has fully unwound, tempered by expected leaner H1 FY2027 months during the DAF Next Generation transition. Management framed the overall posture as 'positioning to adapt to ongoing geopolitical volatility and a slowly improving New Zealand economy.' The 2026 Annual Meeting is scheduled for midday, Friday 6 November 2026, at the Harbourside Function Venue, Wellington.

bull_case: FY2026 trading profit after tax grew 4.7% to $18.7m despite a disrupted H2 (Middle East conflict/oil shock), with revenue up 6.8% to ~$1.07bn, and the Board rewarded shareholders with a total dividend increase to 40cps (70% payout) from 35cps, signalling confidence in earnings durability

Balance sheet materially strengthened over FY2026 (significantly lower inventory, reduced borrowings), giving CMC capacity to fund the coming wave of NEV dealership investment and property development from a position of strength rather than stress

Large owned freehold property portfolio provides real, appreciating collateral value and downside protection largely absent from asset-light auto retailers, plus optionality to develop or realise sites

Accelerating, diversified new-energy-vehicle pivot - Mazda 6e/CX-6e, Ford Ranger Hybrid, JAC T9 PHEV, Next Generation DAF trucks, and an expanding BYD dealership footprint (Canterbury, Wairarapa, Taranaki) - positions CMC to capture the demand shift the oil shock accelerated, rather than being purely a victim of it

Resilient, growing parts/service (aftersales) revenue and a diversified franchise base (Ford/Mazda, Southpac trucks, Agricentre tractors, JAC, Mitsubishi, BYD) reduce reliance on any single model cycle and smooth earnings through downturns
Long, consistent and now-growing dividend history with disciplined family ownership incentivised to protect and grow the payout; insiders have been net buyers of stock over the past year
bear_case: CEO Alex Gibbons' own September 2026 warning that the NZ market has reached an 'unsustainable' level of brand competition (over a dozen Chinese entrants in two years) signals further near-term margin pressure across new and used vehicle sales before any relief from an expected consolidation materialises

H2 FY2026 was directly disrupted by a Middle East conflict/oil-price shock that caught CMC's diesel-weighted inventory flat-footed, illustrating the group's vulnerability to sudden geopolitical and commodity shocks that can rapidly shift demand mix with little warning

Southpac's heavy-truck business remains only tentatively recovering - flat FY2026 volumes, with management explicitly guiding to several 'leaner' months in H1 FY2027 during the DAF model transition, and only 'early signs' (not confirmed data) of a 2027 upturn

Thin free float (Gibbons family >60% ownership) means low liquidity, wide bid/ask spreads, and limited scope for index inclusion or institutional accumulation, which can keep the stock trading at a persistent discount to intrinsic/property-backed value regardless of fundamentals

Management's own framing of FY2027 as merely a 'slowly improving New Zealand economy' amid 'ongoing geopolitical volatility' suggests the recovery narrative remains fragile and non-linear, with FY2026 trading profit growth of only 4.7% (well below the H1-alone growth rate) showing how much ground H2 gave back
